public_rationale: On 20 December 2024, ARC Prize reported that o3 scored 75.7% on the ARC-AGI-1 Semi-Private set within its $10k public leaderboard compute limit. A high-compute configuration scored 87.5% (e1). ARC Prize said ARC-AGI-1 went from 0% with GPT-3 in 2020 to 5% with GPT-4o in 2024, and it called o3's result a breakthrough (e1, e2). TechCrunch reported the same day that o3 solved 25.2% of FrontierMath problems and that no other model exceeded 2%. That figure came from OpenAI's internal evaluations (e3). Both reported results were large jumps over earlier models, so the checkable part of the claim holds. On 18 April 2025, Epoch AI's results put o3 closer to 10% on FrontierMath (e4). TechRepublic said the December test used a prerelease version of o3 and that the problem set had changed since then (e4). That later result concerns a different setup and does not change what was reported at the reveal.
limitations: 'Truly impressive' is a judgment and was not scored.
The December FrontierMath figure was OpenAI's own internal evaluation. The packet has no primary Epoch AI confirmation from that time.
ARC Prize states that the o3 it tested was trained on the ARC-AGI-1 Public Training set. The evidence does not show how this affected the score.
The evidence covers results reported at the reveal. It does not show how the released o3 performs across tasks in general.

our_interpretation: 'Truly impressive' is a judgment and is not scored on its own. The checkable part is whether o3's reported scores on ARC-AGI and FrontierMath at the 20 December 2024 reveal were large jumps over the previous best results.
'Major advance' means a jump well beyond small, step-by-step gains over earlier models.
criteria.support_condition: Scores reported at the reveal show o3 far above earlier models on both ARC-AGI and FrontierMath.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Scores reported at the reveal show only small gains over the previous best, or no gain, on either benchmark.
